title: Rank compatibility for clopen restrictions of finite etale morphisms
statement: Let $q:X\to S$ be finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] and let $(j:X_0\to X,q_0:X_0\to S_0,q,i:S_0\to S)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $W\subseteq X$ be open [def-weil-open-immersion] and closed. Then both $q|_W:W\to S$ and $q_0|_{j^{-1}W}:j^{-1}W\to S_0$ are finite etale. For each $x\in S_0$, the rank of the second morphism at $x$ equals the rank of the first at $i(x)$, in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso].

proof.text: The inclusion of W is an open immersion and has closed image, hence a closed immersion (IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion, ClosedImmersion.lean:65, using Opens.range_ι). It is therefore finite, and also etale. The same applies to j inverse image W, whose closedness follows by continuity. The base change q0 is finite etale; composition gives both claimed properties.

The inverse-image open square is cartesian by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]. Paste it vertically with the given square by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. The resulting square has vertical maps precisely the two restricted projections. Apply the rank base-change equality in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso].

blueprint_update.statement: Let $q:X\to S$ be finite etale and let $(j:X_0\to X,q_0:X_0\to S_0,q,i:S_0\to S)$ be a cartesian square of schemes. Let $W\subseteq X$ be open and closed. Then both $q|_W:W\to S$ and $q_0|_{j^{-1}W}:j^{-1}W\to S_0$ are finite etale. For each $x\in S_0$, the rank of the second morphism at $x$ (the dimension over $\kappa(x)$ of the ring of global sections of its fibre over $x$) equals the rank of the first at $i(x)$.

proof.text: The inclusion $W\to X$ of the clopen subset is an open immersion with closed image, hence also a closed immersion; so it is both etale and finite. The same holds for the inclusion of $j^{-1}W$, which is clopen in $X_0$ by continuity of $j$. The base change $q_0$ of the finite etale morphism $q$ is finite etale, and composites of finite etale morphisms are finite etale. This gives the four finiteness and etaleness claims.

The square formed by $j^{-1}W\to W$, the two inclusions and $j$ is cartesian, since a morphism to $X_0$ factors through $j^{-1}W$ exactly when its composite with $j$ factors through $W$. Pasting it with the given cartesian square gives a cartesian square whose vertical maps are $q_0|_{j^{-1}W}$ and $q|_W$. The rank of a finite flat morphism of finite presentation is invariant under base change in a cartesian square, which gives the asserted equality of ranks. No surjectivity of $i$ is used.
